text.en: Before a race, a cricketer swings her arms and a footballer jogs on the spot. Why? A warm body moves better and is safer.

A warm-up prepares your muscles and joints before play. A cool-down slowly relaxes the body afterwards.
Backward kicks: kneel on hands and knees and kick one leg up behind you, then the other. It strengthens the back and hip muscles.
Side lifts: kneel on hands and knees and lift one leg sideways. It strengthens the hips.
Seated twists: sit, lift your feet a little and twist side to side as if passing a ball. It strengthens the core muscles.
Candle pose: lie on your back and lift your legs straight up; move them gently like fluttering butterflies without bending the knees. Bear crawl hold: hold the bear position on hands and feet with knees off the ground.
Ankle rockers, wide-legged forward fold, inchworm walkout, glute lift, shoulder freehand exercise, reverse tabletop hold, shoulder taps and the side shuffle with a cross are the other activities in the book. Each stretches or strengthens a different part of the body.
Do each movement slowly and stop if it hurts. Breathe normally.

problem.en: Which exercise works the core in the book's warm-up list?

text.en: Look at the exercises that twist or hold the middle of the body.

why.en: Core means the muscles of the tummy and back.

text.en: Seated twists make the core muscles strong.
Candle pose and shoulder taps also strengthen the core.

why.en: Many warm-ups target more than one area.

prompt.en: Why do we warm up before playing?

points.en: Warm up before play and cool down after.
Seated twists, candle pose and bear crawl hold strengthen the core.
Backward kicks and side lifts strengthen the back and hips.
